approach:
Add `jobs::provenance(git, change, judged, history)` in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs. It judges a job's records against cross-links that Athena's own writers always leave. Every refusal is a `Rule::JobRecords` violation whose detail starts with `PROVENANCE` ("provenance: "), names the record path and the missing or contradicting evidence, and whose repair names the Athena command that writes it.

Trigger: the commit adds a closing score (no `cause`) or any outcome of a request job. A request job is any `records/jobs/<month>/<id>/` whose id has `JobId::is_request()`, whether or not job.json or request.json exists (finding 6). A proposal closed with `athena close` has neither a job.json nor a dispatch.

Rules, all read from the change's tree:
- R1, for each reading of the job:
  - request.json exists with `received_at <= reading.at`;
  - a Reader invocation with `seq == reading.invocation_seq` and `ended_at <= reading.at` exists;
  - if `reading.base_commit` is held (`git.rev_parse`), `defaults.toml` at that commit exists and `sha256_hex` of it equals `reading.defaults_sha256`. A base commit that is not held is skipped, not refused: a squash, gc or shallow clone can drop it (findings 4 and 8).
  This refuses the hand-made proposal closed with `athena close` (forgery c) and a whole job written by hand (forgery a).
- R2 and R4, only when the outcome is Landed:
  - job.json exists. The checked dispatch fields are exactly accepted_reading, accepted_by, caps, base_commit, config_sha256, defaults_sha256, athena, driver, brief_sha256 and dispatched_at. request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note, pin and dispatch_branch are not checked (finding 5).
  - The config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's.
  - The verification names a Verifier invocation.
  - Every Producer and Verifier invocation has `started_at >= dispatched_at`.
  - The named verifier starts at or after the `ended_at` of the latest Producer with a lower seq.
  - `outcome.at >= verifier.ended_at`.
  This refuses a forged landing of a dispatched job that never closed (forgery b) when its fields or times contradict the dispatch.

Why no new rule is needed to run it on live commits: `jobs::check` is called from only two live sites (lib.rs:357 and 372, both with history `None`) and from the history walk (history.rs:255, with `Some`). So `jobs::check` becomes `check_records(..)` (the old body, unchanged) plus `provenance(..)` when `history.is_none()`.
- This needs no edit to lib.rs or legacy.rs, which are not deliverables (findings 1 and 2).
- The history walk (`check_history_with_exempt`), and with it the frozen legacy path (legacy.rs:192), is byte-for-byte unchanged (finding 4).

History: `check_after_cutover` also runs `jobs::provenance(.., None)` on each commit of `rev-list --reverse c0..tip`. A hand-written job on main after C0 is judged by CI. The non-cutover walk and the pre-C0 commits are not judged by it.

Dropped from the earlier plan: R3 (job.json added before its reading is in the parent). It refused the genuine fixture `seed_accepted_jobs` (run/tests.rs:1413), and a forger can satisfy it by adding two commits (finding 3).

No record field is added. records.rs and reconcile.rs stay untouched. Tests go in the existing landing_tests.rs plus one in history.rs.

decisions.choice: Wire the live gate through `jobs::check`: split it into `check_records` (the old body) and `check`, which adds `provenance` only when `history` is `None`.
decisions.reason: The two live gate sites (lib.rs:357 and 372) pass `None`; the history walk (history.rs:255) passes `Some(state)`. So the live gate gains the check, and the frozen legacy path (legacy.rs:192 -> check_history_with_exempt) and every pre-C0 judgment stay identical, with no edit to lib.rs or legacy.rs (not in the reading's deliverables). `check`'s doc comment states that `None` means a commit being made.

rejected.option: Call `jobs::provenance` from `gate()` in lib.rs and add a legacy.rs test
rejected.why: lib.rs and legacy.rs are not deliverables; findings 1 and 2 flag the wider scope.

rejected.option: Put the checks into `check_records` for every caller
rejected.why: Re-judges frozen pre-C0 records that older builds wrote without dispatch fields, and the exempt list cannot grow.
Edits invariant.rs for no gain over the None/Some split.

decisions.choice: Do not run provenance in the non-cutover history walk. Run it in the live gate and in a new loop over `c0..tip` in `check_after_cutover`.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: with no `[history] cutover_job`, walking all history would refuse genuine older jobs (dispatch fields are Options, records.rs:607-633) and squash-landed jobs whose base commit is gone, and `[history] exempt` is keyed by sha so the owner has no remedy. Commits after C0 come from builds that write the fields, and the loop reuses the same function.

rejected.option: walk(.., provenance=true) on the cutover_job == None branch
rejected.why: The round-2 design; refuses genuine old history (finding 4).
A person can skip the commit hook; CI after C0 is a cheap second line.

decisions.choice: Drop R3 (job.json before its reading) and cover forgery (a) with R1, plus R2 on a Landed outcome.
decisions.reason: R3 refuses `seed_accepted_jobs` (run/tests.rs:1413-1451), which commits Request, Reading and Job in one `commit_records` call through the gate (finding 3). It also tells little, since a forger can add two commits. R1's request record, reader invocation and defaults hash, and R2's dispatch fields, are what a hand-made job lacks. With R3 gone, no run/tests.rs edit is needed: that fixture adds no closing score or outcome, so the trigger does not fire.

rejected.option: Keep R3 and change the fixture to commit the reading first
rejected.why: Edits a non-deliverable test file for a weak signal, and every `commit_records` caller that seeds readings and job.json together would need the same change.

decisions.choice: R2 and R4 apply only to a Landed outcome; R1 applies to any closing. Required dispatch fields are the exact list in the approach; dispatch_branch and the null-in-genuine fields are not required.
decisions.reason: Findings 4 and 5. `athena close` on an open job dispatched by an older build (abandoned, not Landed) must still work; genuine dispatches write request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note and pin as null (run/mod.rs:983-988; records.rs:626-633). Forgery (b) is a landing, so R2/R4 sit where it lives.

rejected.option: Require every dispatch field on every closing
rejected.why: Refuses genuine jobs and old-build jobs.

decisions.choice: A reading whose `base_commit` is not held is not refused. The `defaults_sha256` comparison is skipped for it, and the docs list this as a residual.
decisions.reason: Finding 8 and the host squash-merge fact: the commit can be gone after a reset, gc or shallow checkout, and the live gate has no remedy. The request record and reader invocation still gate the proposal. Only a held base lets `defaults_sha256` be recomputed exactly (capability.rs:51).

rejected.option: Refuse a base commit that is not held

rejected.why: It hashes `Config::reading_inputs()` (capability.rs:45), which follows the writing build's code; it is only compared between job.json and the accepted reading.

decisions.choice: The verifier is ordered against the latest producer with a lower seq, not all producers. No producer is required.
decisions.reason: A retry makes a second producer start after the first verifier. A resumed kept candidate may have no producer in the records.

decisions.choice: State forgery (b) as detected only when its fields or times contradict the dispatch. A consistent forgery passes; a test records that limit.
decisions.reason: No committed value binds the closing records to the dispatch that a forger cannot compute; signing is out of scope. Saying so plainly is more useful than a stronger claim.

crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs feeds request and reading text through the reading checkers. This plan adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check. The input forms are record shapes, mapped to the new landing_tests.rs tests: (a), (b), (c), the genuine landing and the older-build job. The producer and verifier still run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a no-regression command; I cite no case ids and no result.

rejected.option: Corpus cases for forged record shapes
rejected.why: The corpus runs request text, not commit records.

decisions.choice: Leave records.rs and reconcile.rs untouched although the brief lists them.
decisions.reason: Every link used is already stored: Reading base_commit/defaults_sha256/invocation_seq/at, Request.received_at, the Job dispatch fields, and Invocation role/seq/started_at/ended_at. Outcome totals are already reconciled with invocation sums by reconcile.rs. A new witness field would be one a forger recomputes, and it would add allow-list surface.

rejected.option: Chain hash or witness field on Score or Outcome
rejected.why: Recomputable by the forger; real signing is out of scope.

risks.risk: A real writer's records fail a new link (a false refusal), for example a reading without a reader invocation or a timestamp ordering that is not what I read.
risks.mitigation: Step 1 re-reads the writers; reading.rs:788 is the only production `Reading` constructor. Comparisons are one-directional and ties pass. The lifecycle, job_plan and drain suites run real writers through the live gate. Step 7 treats a failure there as a bug in the check.

risks.risk: A genuine job dispatched by an older build lacks a required dispatch field and is refused when it lands after an upgrade, with no sha-keyed exempt remedy in the live gate.
risks.mitigation: Only a Landed outcome is held to dispatch fields. The required list is limited to the ten fields that the reading, dispatch and ordering rules use, and dispatch_branch is not required. Closes of open or old jobs (abandoned, dropped) face R1 only. The docs name the case.

risks.risk: A hand-built gated fixture elsewhere in the workspace adds a reading with a closing record and is refused.
risks.mitigation: The grep over `commit_records` callers found none (see dependents). Step 7 runs the whole workspace; a failure is fixed in that fixture alone and listed.

risks.risk: Forgery (b) with consistent times, or a fully mimicked job, passes. The docs could be read as stronger than they are.
risks.mitigation: The docs and CHANGELOG say so plainly. A control test (`..._with_consistent_times_still_passes`) records the limit.

risks.risk: Job records written only to the athena/records branch are not judged by this check.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a residual in the docs and CHANGELOG. Main commits are judged by the live gate and the post-C0 loop. See the open question.

risks.risk: A base commit that is not held (gc, reset, shallow clone) skips the defaults hash comparison, so a forger could name a bogus base to skip it.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a residual. The request record and reader invocation checks still apply to every reading.

demonstrations.method:
Run the athena-gate suite. New tests in landing_tests.rs build real temporary git repositories. They call `jobs::provenance` through a new helper, and the live `crate::gate` for the wiring, and assert the Violations. A history.rs test covers the post-C0 loop.
(a) `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`:
  - commit 1 adds the old all-null `opening(&HONEST)` (reading, job.json, reader invocation); `provenance_of` is empty there because nothing closes;
  - commit 2 adds the code and `closing(fp)` (Landed); assert violations with detail containing "no request record" and a missing dispatch field, and repair containing "athena ask" / "athena go".
  - A second variant has full genuine evidence except the request record.
(b) `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused`:
  - genuine Read commit (request, reading, reader invocation) and Dispatch commit (full job.json), then one forged commit with the code and closing records.
  - Five variants, each breaking one link: a producer started before `dispatched_at`; the verifier started before the producer ended; the outcome before the verifier ended; `dispatched_at` missing; the job's defaults hash differing from the reading's.
  - A control with consistent times is accepted (`..._with_consistent_times_still_passes`), recording the stated limit.
(c) `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused`:
  - a reading with invented forecasts, no request record, no reader invocation and no job.json, closed by a Score plus a Dropped outcome (the shape of manage.rs:195-207); assert "no request record" and "no reader invocation";
  - the same commit through `crate::gate(git, &change, Scope::CommitMsg)` contains a violation whose detail starts with "provenance: ";
  - a control with request, reader invocation, held base and matching defaults hash is accepted.
(d) `the_older_build_job_in_a_non_cutover_history_is_not_refused`: the old-shape fixture from (a) with an unreachable base commit; `history_of(&git)` has no violation starting "provenance: ", while `provenance_of` on its closing commit does refuse (the fixture triggers).
history.rs cutover_tests: `provenance_is_judged_on_main_commits_after_c0` uses `world(true)`, `record_cutover` and `record_landing`, adds a commit holding `landing_tests::hand_made_proposal()` records, and asserts `flagged(&report, &forged)` has a detail starting "provenance: " while `hand` has none.
Existing genuine-landing tests still pass.
demonstrations.observes: Each forged history gives at least one `Rule::JobRecords` Violation whose detail starts `provenance: ` and names the evidence. The controls, the genuine landing, the older-build history walk and the pre-C0 comparison give none. All existing landing, chain, intervention and exemption tests pass, with `job_records_of` and jobs.rs `check_head` now calling `check_records`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base code `jobs::check` never reads the request record, the reader invocation, the dispatch fields, defaults.toml at the base or the invocation times. Tests (a), (b), (c) and the post-C0 test therefore fail on `!violations.is_empty()` and on the `detail.contains(..)` assertions. Without the `history.is_none()` call in `check`, the `Scope::CommitMsg` assertion in (c) fails. Without the c0..tip loop the history.rs test fails. If provenance ran in the plain walk, (d) fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `crate::jobs::provenance` via a new helper `provenance_of(git, rev)` that builds `Change::of_commit` and `Judged::new` like the existing `job_records_of` (landing_tests.rs:823); `crate::gate(.., Scope::CommitMsg)`; `crate::history::check_history` via the existing `history_of` (landing_tests.rs:306); `check_after_cutover` via the history.rs `world`/`record_cutover` helpers. Fixture: real temporary git repositories from `testutil::{repo, write, commit}` and `owner_repo`. Plan step 5 adds `genuine_repo` (owner_repo plus a committed defaults.toml), `genuine_reading`, `genuine_job` (JSON text with all dispatch fields, like `job_record`), `request_record`, `provenance_of` and `hand_made_proposal` (pub(crate)). Existing: `write_records`, `opening`, `closing`, `stage_landing`, `history_of`. Nothing in the gate is stubbed.

demonstrations.method: Run clippy, fmt and the workspace tests. The workspace run compiles and runs the athena-core and athena-cli suites. The lifecycle and job_plan tests drive real ask/go/close through the fake driver (athena-agent fake.rs, real clocks at lines 95 and 123) and the production writers through `gate()`, so the new links are shown to hold for Athena's own records. The fixture `seed_accepted_jobs` (run/tests.rs:1413) and code_health `close_job` (code_health.rs:1155) commit through the gate but add no reading with a closing record, so they are not triggered.
demonstrations.command: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets && cargo fmt --check && cargo test --workspace
demonstrations.observes: No diagnostics, no formatting diff, all tests pass, including the lifecycle tests that close real proposals and land real jobs and the policy and prompt-budget tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: Not a refusal behavior. A warning, a formatting difference, or a genuine writer's records failing the new check (a false refusal in lifecycle, job_plan or drain) fails these commands.
demonstrations.seam: Production binaries and test targets run as they are. No double. Existing.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused` in landing_tests.rs builds the shape Athena writes, with the genuine helpers. Commit 1 'Read' adds request.json, a reading with the repository's real `base_commit` and `defaults_sha256`, and the reader invocation. Commit 2 'Dispatch' adds a full job.json. Commit 3 adds the code, producer and verifier invocations in order, candidate, verification and a Landed outcome. It asserts `provenance_of` is empty for each commit and that `history_of(&git)` has no violation starting "provenance: ". The same suite includes the unchanged existing landing tests, which are genuine shapes. The verifier also runs the lifecycle suite, whose real writers are the repository's real history shape, and the refusal corpus as a no-regression check.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-gate && cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: No provenance violation on any genuine commit or on the walk, so refusal is by missing or contradicting evidence, not blanket. The share of the repository's real past jobs newly refused is not measured, because records/ is absent from the snapshot and the history file omits it; the 5% is the request's estimate. The live gate sees only new commits, and pre-C0 history is not re-judged at all.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check refused genuine records, `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused` and the lifecycle tests fail. If no check existed, the criterion 1 forged tests fail.
demonstrations.seam: `provenance_of` and `history_of` on a real temporary repository with genuine-shaped helpers (added in step 5). The lifecycle suite uses the existing Fixture and fake driver with the production writers.

demonstrations.method: The criterion 1 tests assert on `detail` and `repair` text. A Grep checks the source: every violation in `jobs::provenance` is built by one local `fail(path, detail, repair)` whose detail begins with the `PROVENANCE` constant, and each call site names the missing or contradicting evidence and the Athena command that writes it.
demonstrations.observes: Assertions such as `detail.contains("no request record")`, `"no reader invocation"`, `"does not match defaults.toml"`, `"has no job.json"`, `"lacks dispatched_at"`, `"before the job was dispatched"`, `"before the producer invocation ended"` and `"before the verifier invocation ended"`, and `repair.contains("athena ask")` / `"athena go"` / `"athena close"`, pass. `Grep "provenance: " crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs` lists the texts; history.rs adds no text (the post-C0 loop reuses these violations).
demonstrations.fails_without: A generic message such as 'records are not valid' fails the `contains` assertions in each forged test.
demonstrations.seam: The `Violation { detail, repair, path }` values returned by `jobs::provenance`, read through `provenance_of`. Existing type; assertions added in step 5.

demonstrations.method: Content check on the diff. §16.2 of docs/design/athena-v0.md ('Records are not signed' and the table row near line 1964 that calls detection a queued request) and docs/enforcement.md (the M27 row near line 41 and the 'Records are Athena's own' bullet near lines 71-78) are rewritten. They list the evidence each of the three forgeries now has to carry and name the new tests. They say where the check runs: the live gate (commit-msg hook, `athena close`, every Athena commit) and main commits after C0. They state the residuals: (1) consistent, fully mimicked records still pass because nothing is signed; (2) forgery (b) is caught only when its fields or times contradict the dispatch; (3) job records written only to the athena/records branch are not judged; (4) pre-C0 history and the non-cutover history walk are not re-judged; (5) a base commit that is not held skips the defaults hash comparison.
demonstrations.observes: The old text saying the three forgeries pass is replaced by the detected cases and residuals. Every test name the docs cite is found by Grep in landing_tests.rs or history.rs.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no doc edit the diff is empty and the 'still passes' text remains.
demonstrations.seam: Not applicable: content criterion on documentation. Step 8 makes the edit.

demonstrations.method: Content check: one new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` in CHANGELOG.md names the provenance check, the three forgeries, where it runs (the live gate and main after C0), that earlier history is not re-judged, forgery (b)'s limit, and the residual that consistent forgeries pass without signing.
demonstrations.observes: A new Unreleased bullet describes the detection and the residual.
demonstrations.fails_without: No Unreleased entry appears in the diff.
demonstrations.seam: Not applicable: content criterion. Step 9 makes the edit.

demonstrations.method: The verifier checks that no record field or governance file changed. The provenance code reads only existing fields. The athena-data tests that hold the allow-list and round-trip coverage run unchanged, since no field is added.
demonstrations.observes: The diff lists only crates/athena-gate/src/{jobs,history,landing_tests}.rs, docs/design/athena-v0.md, docs/enforcement.md and CHANGELOG.md. None of athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows, setup.sh, prompt files, records/, crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs, lib.rs or legacy.rs appears. The athena-data tests (check_record_file and the AnyRecord round-trip) pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A new record field without allow-list and round-trip coverage fails `cargo test -p athena-data`; an edit to a governance file shows in the stat.
demonstrations.seam: The repository diff and the existing athena-data tests. Existing; nothing is added.

open_questions: User: Job records written only to the athena/records branch (records-history.md stage 1) are not judged by this check, and the branch's only audit is append-only. Should a follow-up job run the provenance check on that branch's commits? It needs a layout adapter for its root-level paths. I recommend yes.
